name: f
statement: theorem f (n : Nat) : False
proof:
:= f n
  ```

  ```
  fail to show termination for
    f
  with errors
  failed to infer structural recursion:
  Not considering parameter n of f:
    it is unchanged in the recursive calls
  no parameters suitable for structural recursion

  well-founded recursion cannot be used, `f` does not take any (non-fixed)
  arguments
  ```

  If we were allowed to write that function, we could use it to prove `False`:

  ```
  theorem paradox : False := f 0
  ```

  To prevent this, Lean requires that recursive functions have some argument
  which is structurally "decreasing" at every recursive call. Lean can
  automatically figure out which argument that is.

name: flip_flop
statement: theorem flip_flop (proof : MyProp) : MyProp
proof:
:=
  match proof with
  | .proof1 => .proof2
  | .proof2 => .proof1

name: successors_equal
statement: theorem successors_equal n1 n2 : n1 = n2 → Nat.succ n1 = Nat.succ n2
proof:
:=
  fun h =>
    match n2, h with
    | _, .refl _ => .refl _

name: successor_injective
statement: theorem successor_injective n1 n2 : Nat.succ n1 = Nat.succ n2 → n1 = n2
proof:
:=
  fun h =>
    match h with
    | .refl _ => .refl _

name: true_neq_false
statement: theorem true_neq_false : true ≠ false
proof:
:= 
  fun h =>
    match (motive := ∀ z, true = z → if z then True else False) false, h with
    | _, .refl _ => True.intro

name: n_plus_zero_equals_n
statement: theorem n_plus_zero_equals_n n : n + 0 = n
proof: := Eq.refl n

name: zero_plus_n_equals_n
statement: theorem zero_plus_n_equals_n n : 0 + n = n
proof:
:= Eq.refl n
  ```

  ```
  Type mismatch
    Eq.refl n
  has type
    n = n
  but is expected to have type
    0 + n = n
  ```

  ```
  example : ∀ n, 0 + n = n := by
    intro n
    rfl
  ```

  ```
  Tactic `rfl` failed: The left-hand side
    0 + n
  is not definitionally equal to the right-hand side
    n
  ```

name: zero_plus_n_equals_n
statement: theorem zero_plus_n_equals_n n : 0 + n = n
proof:
:=
  match n with
  | .zero => Eq.refl _
  | .succ p =>
    match
      (motive := ∀x, 0 + p = x → 0 + Nat.succ p = Nat.succ x)
      p, zero_plus_n_equals_n p
    with
    | _, .refl _ => .refl _

name: commutativity
statement: theorem commutativity (n1 n2 : Nat) : n1 + n2 = n2 + n1
proof:
:= by
  induction n2 with
  | zero =>
    rw [zero_plus_n_equals_n] 
    rfl
  | succ p1 h1 =>
    change (n1 + p1) + 1 = p1 + 1 + n1 
    rw [h1]
    clear h1 
    induction n1 with 
    | zero => rfl
    | succ p2 h2 =>
      change p1 + p2 + 1 + 1 = p1 + 1 + (p2 + 1)
      rw [h2]
      rfl

name: sub_middle
statement:
@[local simp] theorem sub_middle (n1 n2 n3 : Nat) :
  n1 + n2 + n3 - n2 = n1 + n3
proof:
:= by
  rw [Nat.add_assoc]
  rw (occs := .pos [2]) [Nat.add_comm]
  rw [← Nat.add_assoc]
  simp

name: modus_ponens
statement: theorem modus_ponens (α β : Prop) : (α → β) → α → β
proof:
:=
  fun h1 h2 => h1 h2

name: true_and_true_1
statement: theorem true_and_true_1 : True ∧ True
proof: := And.intro True.intro True.intro

name: true_and_true_2
statement: theorem true_and_true_2 : True ∧ True
proof:
:= by
  /-
    Use `apply` to prove the goal via some known fact. In this case, we'll use
    the fact that we can prove a conjunction by proving each half individually.
  -/
  apply And.intro
  . apply True.intro 
  . apply True.intro

name: true_and_true_3
statement: theorem true_and_true_3 : True ∧ True
proof:
:= by
  apply And.intro <;> apply True.intro

name: conjunction_symmetric
statement: theorem conjunction_symmetric α β : α ∧ β → β ∧ α
proof:
:=
  fun h1 =>
    match h1 with
    | .intro h2 h3 => ⟨h3, h2⟩

name: disjunction_symmetric
statement: theorem disjunction_symmetric α β : (α ∨ β) → (β ∨ α)
proof:
:=
  fun h1 =>
    match h1 with
    | .inl h2 => .inr h2
    | .inr h2 => .inl h2

name: iff_symmetric
statement: theorem iff_symmetric α β : (α ↔ β) → (β ↔ α)
proof:
:=
  fun h => Iff.intro h.mpr h.mp

name: explosion
statement: theorem explosion (α : Prop) : False → α
proof:
:=
  fun h =>
    nomatch h

name: one_plus_one_equals_two
statement: theorem one_plus_one_equals_two : 1 + 1 = 2
proof: := Eq.refl 2

name: eq_symmetric
statement: theorem eq_symmetric α (x y : α) : x = y → y = x
proof:
:=
  fun h =>
    match h with
    | Eq.refl _ => Eq.refl x

name: eq_transitive
statement: theorem eq_transitive α (x y z : α) : x = y → y = z → x = z
proof:
:=
  fun h1 h2 =>
    match h2 with
    | .refl _ => h1

name: not_involution
statement: theorem not_involution (b : Bool) : not (not b) = b
proof:
:=
  match b with
  | true => .refl true
  | false => .refl false

name: weird
statement:
theorem weird (f : Nat → Nat) :
  (∀ x, f x = x + 1) →
  ∀ x, f x + 1 = x + 2
proof:
:=
  fun h1 x =>
    match (motive := ∀ z, f x = z → f x + 1 = z + 1) x + 1, h1 x with
    | _, .refl _ => .refl _

name: half_of_6_exists
statement: theorem half_of_6_exists : ∃ x, 2 * x = 6
proof:
:=
  ⟨3, Eq.refl 6⟩

name: divisible_by_4_implies_even
statement: theorem divisible_by_4_implies_even x : (∃ y, 4 * y = x) → (∃ z, 2 * z = x)
proof:
:=
  fun ⟨y, h2⟩ =>
    ⟨
      2 * y,
      match
        (motive := ∀ z, ((2 * 2) * y = z) → z = x)
        _, Nat.mul_assoc 2 2 y
      with
      | _, .refl _ => h2
    ⟩
